This article compares the performance of Danish regions and hospital departments regarding Indicator 4: the proportion of patients with [[ibd|IBD]] in treatment with [[bmsl|Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] (BMSL) who have fecal [[calprotectin|calprotectin]] (F-calpro) measured at least once a year. The data, sourced from the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]], evaluates whether departments meet the national target of 80% compliance [^src1]. Because the available evidence consists of a single snapshot from 2023, no longitudinal trends can be established; the analysis is strictly cross-sectional [^src1].

Nationally, Denmark missed the 80% target, achieving a compliance rate of 78% (8,199 out of 10,523 patients) [^src1]. At the regional level, only Region Sjælland met the standard, scoring 94% [^src1]. The remaining regions fell short: Region Syddanmark (79%), Region Midtjylland (76%), Region Nordjylland (76%), and Region Hovedstaden (73%) [^src1]. 

The data reveals a stark contrast between pediatric and adult departments, making pediatrics a clear leader category. Several pediatric departments achieved perfect or near-perfect compliance, including SUH Roskilde Pædiatri (100%, 24/24), OUH Odense Børne- og Ungeafdeling H (100%, 61/61), SLB Kolding Børne- og Ungeafdeling (100%, 25/25), and Hvidovre Børne- og Ungeafdelingen (99%, 144/145) [^src1]. Conversely, the lowest-performing departments (the trailers) are predominantly adult gastroenterology or medical units. The most extreme outlier is Rigshospitalet Med. Klinik Mave-, Tarm- og Leversygd., which recorded a mere 13% compliance rate (38/286), drastically underperforming compared to both the national average and its own region [^src1]. Other notable trailers include Nordsjælland Kirurgisk overafdeling (52%), SLB Vejle Medicinsk Afdeling (56%), and Aarhus Lever-, Mave- og Tarmsygdomme (61%) [^src1].

Summary: Tabellen viser regional og afdelingsvis opfyldelse af indikator 4 (årlig F-calpro-måling hos patienter med IBD i BMSL-behandling), hvor Sjælland og flere pædiatriske afdelinger opnår >90 %, mens nogle store centrale enheder som Rigshospitalet ligger langt under målsætningen på 80 %.
